title: world.counters gpu reports the world's view as a render-graph instance of the sdf.world passes, pass by pass in order, rendered once for a still world and identically on both backends
binding: The positive leg boots a still offscreen world with one SDF view, waits for the engine to be ready (world.wait ready: the world's residency has built its tables and the root has rendered over the world's first output), and reads the gpu section of world.counters sixty completed ticks later and again after thirty more. The world's view is the render-graph instance world, whose node renders the sdf.world package's ten passes; the residency's uploads read as sdf:world. Nothing the view renders from changes in a still world, so the scheduler lets its first render stand for every later frame: the world node's submission is the same in both reads, while the root, main, renders every frame, so its second read carries a later submission. The world node's pass lines appear in the fragment's order, sky through views, each carrying the barriers the planner planned for it and the write of its pass block, and none a command buffer: every pass records into the node's one list a frame, which the outside line counts; the mesh pass skips the frame, because the world draws no mesh, so its line is empty and its target and depth take no barrier; the ambient and shadow passes skip it too, because the world leaves ambient occlusion and soft shadows off, so their lines are empty. Those pass lines are exact on Vulkan and Direct3D 12 alike, which is the cross-backend proof. The residency's upload line, the work outside the passes and the created buffers, pools and sets follow the device's residency policy (a staging device records copies, transitions and copy sets beside the writes), so the canary names those lines without pinning them. Neither node creates a pipeline or a shader module: every pipeline counts under gpu.pass-pipelines, fifteen pipelines and sixteen shader modules (the eleven SDF kernels the world's residency leases, the brick baker absent from the counters kernels, the device's region copy, the one place pipeline the root's four place passes share, and the mesh pass's graphics pipeline with its vertex and fragment modules). The residency creates two images, its sampled and storage fillers, and the world node five (its output in each of three frame slots, and the mesh pass's visibility target and depth, one each, which every frame slot shares). The root places the world's one view through its four place passes, none of which shows anything, so none dispatches and each pass line carries only its planned barriers. The discriminating leg reads world.counters gpu twice before the first tick, when no submission has completed, so neither read shows a pass line and the positive's exact lines turn red.
